newsitem.title: NORWAY: Justice Minister Anne Holt quits Norway government. [CORRECTED 12:32 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Justice Minister Anne Holt quits Norway government. [CORRECTED 12:32 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects Holt's given name, in headline and text, to Anne from Anna)
Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland announced on Tuesday that Justice Minister Anne Holt had resigned from the minority Labour government on grounds of illness.
Holt, who has been on sick leave for several weeks suffering from anaemia, joined the government when it was formed last October.
Gerd-Liv Valla, deputy chairwoman of the Civil Servants Union, was named to succeed her (Corrects from him).
Jagland, who is also Labour Party chairman, has encountered major difficulties since succeeding veteran premier Gro Harlem Brundtland, who resigned on October 25.
Two key cabinet members -- National Planning Minister Terje Roed-Larsen and Energy Minister Grete Faremo -- have resigned in separate scandals.

Roed-Larsen, who quit as a U.N.-appointed Middle East mediator to join the new government, resigned on November 27 amid a storm of media criticism over alleged irregularities in a share option deal he profited from 10 years ago.
On December 16, Oil and Energy Minister Grete Faremo was forced by Jagland to step down in a scandal over the national intelligence service's surveillance of a prominent left-wing politician.

Faremo was justice minister when the intelligence service in June last year started looking for dirt in the background of Berge Furre, a member of a parliamentary committee assigned to examine the work of the intelligence service itself.
